query: meta-agent modifies training environment during multi-turn reinforcement learning
text:
1. **[EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16523)** (October 2026) — **Closest match.** A meta-agent monitors multi-turn RL training and modifies the environment, user simulator, rewards, and training configuration, with validated changes applied during the ongoing run. **People:** Min Cai (University of Alberta); Dan Zhang (National University of Singapore); Gao Xing and Libin Ma (Kuaishou Technology); Zhaohui Xu (independent researcher); Xi Ye (University of Alberta and Alberta Machine Intelligence Institute).

2. **[Weak-for-Strong: Training Weak Meta-Agent to Harness Strong Executors](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.04785)** (April 2025) — Related work that trains a smaller meta-agent using multi-turn RL to iteratively design and refine workflows for stronger models. Its focus is workflow optimization rather than modifying a live training environment. **People:** Fan Nie, Haotian Ye, Weixin Liang, Pan Lu, and James Zou (Stanford University); Lan Feng and Alexandre Alahi (EPFL); Huaxiu Yao (University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill).

query: within-run and across-run adaptation agent training
text:
1. **[Agent-R: Training Language Model Agents to Reflect via Iterative Self-Training](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.11425v3)** (2025). Closest match connecting both timescales: iterative training teaches agents to recognize and correct errors during execution. **People:** Siyu Yuan, Zehui Chen, Zhiheng Xi, Junjie Ye, Zhengyin Du, and Jiecao Chen. **Affiliations:** Fudan University and ByteDance Seed.

2. **[Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=vAElhFcKW6)** (2023). Agents reflect on feedback and retain textual memories to improve subsequent trials, without updating model weights. **People and affiliations:** Noah Shinn and Federico Cassano—Northeastern University; Ashwin Gopinath—MIT; Karthik Narasimhan and Shunyu Yao—Princeton University.

3. **[Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models](https://voyager.minedojo.org/)** (2023). Combines feedback-driven revision during execution with a persistent library of skills reusable across tasks and new Minecraft worlds. **People and affiliations:** Guanzhi Wang and Anima Anandkumar—NVIDIA/Caltech; Yuqi Xie—UT Austin; Yunfan Jiang—Stanford; Ajay Mandlekar and Linxi “Jim” Fan—NVIDIA; Chaowei Xiao—NVIDIA/ASU; Yuke Zhu—NVIDIA/UT Austin.

4. **[ADaPT: As-Needed Decomposition and Planning with Language Models](https://allenai.github.io/adaptllm/)** (2023). Relevant to within-run adaptation: agents recursively decompose subtasks when execution fails. **People and affiliations:** Archiki Prasad and Mohit Bansal—UNC Chapel Hill; Alexander Koller and Mareike Hartmann—Saarland University; Peter Clark, Ashish Sabharwal, and Tushar Khot—Allen Institute for AI.

1. **[SEAL: Synergistic Co-Evolution of Agents and Learning Environments](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.24426)** — May 2026. Jointly adapts tool-use agents and their learning interfaces using diagnosed failures. **People:** Yihao Hu, Zhihao Wen, Xiujin Liu, Pan Wang, Xin Zhang, Wei Wu. **Affiliations:** Ant Group, Westlake University, University of Michigan–Ann Arbor, and University of Science and Technology of China.

2. **[COvolve: Adversarial Co-Evolution of Large-Language-Model-Generated Policies and Environments via Two-Player Zero-Sum Game](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28386)** — March 2026. LLMs generate policies and environments that challenge and improve each other through an adversarial game. **People:** Alkis Sygkounas, Rishi Hazra, Andreas Persson, Pedro Zuidberg Dos Martires, Amy Loutfi. **Affiliation:** Machine Perception and Interaction Lab, Örebro University, Sweden.

3. **[GenEnv: Difficulty-Aligned Co-Evolution Between LLM Agents and Environment Simulators](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.19682)** — December 2025. Trains a generative simulator to produce tasks matched to an agent’s changing capabilities. **People and affiliations:** Jiacheng Guo, Jiahao Qiu, Mengdi Wang — Princeton; Ling Yang — Princeton and ByteDance Seed; Peter Chen — Columbia; Qixin Xiao and Xinzhe Juan — University of Michigan; Yinjie Wang — University of Chicago; Ke Shen — ByteDance Seed.

query: LLM agent training environment evolves with policy
text:

4. **[CoMap: Co-Evolving World Models and Agent Policies for LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.02372)** — Related work in which a textual world model adapts alongside the policy through on-policy interaction. **People:** Youwei Liu (Central South University), Jian Wang (Sichuan University), and Hanlin Wang and Wenjie Li (The Hong Kong Polytechnic University).

query: multi-turn reinforcement learning user simulation benchmarks
text:
1. **[LMRL Gym: Benchmarks for Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning with Language Models](https://lmrl-gym.github.io/)** (2023). Eight tasks for evaluating multi-turn RL, including information gathering and negotiation with LLM-simulated users. **People:** Marwa Abdulhai, Isadora White, Charlie Snell, Charles Sun, Joey Hong, Yuexiang Zhai, and Sergey Levine — UC Berkeley; Kelvin Xu — Google DeepMind.

2. **[UserRL: Training Interactive User-Centric Agent via Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.19736v1)** (2025). 3. **[τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.12045v1)** (2024). Evaluates agents through multi-turn conversations with simulated customers and API tools in retail and airline settings. **People:** Shunyu Yao, Noah Shinn, Pedram Razavi, and Karthik Narasimhan — Sierra; Yao’s work was conducted during an internship.

4. **[MUA-RL: Multi-turn User-interacting Agent Reinforcement Learning for Agentic Tool Use](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.18669v1)** (2025). A related training framework integrating simulated users into RL, evaluated on τ-bench, τ²-bench, and other tool-use benchmarks. **People:** Weikang Zhao — Meituan and Chinese Academy of Sciences; Xili Wang — Meituan and Peking University; Chengdi Ma — Peking University; Lingbin Kong and colleagues — Meituan.

Qiu, and Yuqing Yang — Microsoft Research.
